focus: Map completion-evidence judgment reuse points in .skilled, then define a default-on integration boundary with measurable operating cost and explicit privacy, latency, and authority limits.
noveltyJustification: Three concrete reuse/integration findings are new; two extend previously identified call-volume and evidence limitations to live operation.
keyQuestions: Where else in .skilled would evidence-backed completion judgment help?
What would default-on integration require, cost and risk?
answeredQuestions: Existing closure gates and runtime hooks are reuse points; model integration remains conditional on a later keep and named reader.

ruledOut.approach: Enable model judgment by default in all completion hooks now
ruledOut.reason: The measured arm stopped at the margin gate and feature 026 explicitly defers live judgment pending a keep and named reader.

ruledOut.approach: Use the current regex as an upstream filter for an improved model
ruledOut.reason: All ten reported positive labels were missed by the regex, so that route would discard the cases the model must recover.

title: The evidence core already spans six runtime adapters and is advisory-only
summary: The same runtime-neutral completion evidence core serves Claude, Codex, Devin, Cursor, Pi and OpenCode; adapters differ in text/spec-folder extraction and delivery. The concern is enabled by default but only logs warnings and never blocks.

title: Evidence-backed judgment has direct value at explicit closure gates
summary: System-spec-kit requires check-completion.sh before saying done; unmet acceptance criteria block packet closure; the manual-testing workflow requires validation output before its success claim. These narrow, objective surfaces are stronger reuse points than a blanket model judge on every assistant turn.

title: A default-on model judge is not supported by the current verdict or feature contract
summary: The measured result is stop (margin); the feature spec says live judgment requires a later phase, a keep, and a named reader, and a keep still does not serve anything automatically. The existing regex hook being enabled by default must not be mistaken for approval to ship an online Jev arm.

title: Future serving needs explicit consent, bounded asynchronous work, and a real reader
summary: The audit payload is operator session text; the spec requires secret stripping and --accept-payload before Jev. Current completion advisories are designed never to block, and injection-contract.md says they do not enter model context. A future model arm should retain non-blocking fail-open behavior, expose a kill switch and dedup, send the smallest consented tail, and route its evidence to a named reader. Because the regex missed all ten labeled claims, a regex-only gate cannot be the recall path.

title: Live cost and latency are unknown; the offline run gives a call-count baseline
summary: The 110-row Jev evaluation entails 331 planned calls under the existing three-rerun contract. Each row's full tail is sent on every rerun; dollar cost and live hook rate are not in evidence. The offline judgment timeout is 90 seconds per spawn, while the sentinel bounded check uses 1200 ms; a live integration needs a separate latency budget and telemetry for calls, tokens, p50/p95, timeout rate and observed warning usefulness.
